headline_marked: Shadman Islam [[left stranded on 99]] as bad light stops play in Mirpur Test
headline: Shadman Islam left stranded on 99 as bad light stops play in Mirpur Test
summary: Shadman Islam was denied a century by fading light on Wednesday, finishing unbeaten on 99 as Bangladesh reached 213 for three against the West Indies on day one of the Mirpur Test.
details: Shadman Islam came within a whisker of a century, holding Bangladesh’s innings together through a testing day against West Indies before fading light denied him another chance to reach the landmark. He ended unbeaten on 99, with Bangladesh at 213 for three after 74 overs in the Mirpur Test on Wednesday.

It was only the 20th time in Test cricket that a batter had finished a day on 99 not out. Mushfiqur Rahim, against Ireland last year, was the only other Bangladesh batter to do so. Each of the previous 19 batters went on to complete a century.

Shadman faced 219 balls and struck 10 fours, showing patience against a new ball that offered the West Indies seamers movement and bounce. Tanzid Hasan managed just seven before edging Jayden Seales to Justin Greaves at second slip.

Shadman then added 59 for the second wicket with Mominul Haque, who fell before lunch for a rash shot, advancing to Jomel Warrican and slicing a catch to Shamar Joseph at mid-off. Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto soon departed for 19, trapped lbw by Warrican while attempting a paddle sweep.

Towhid Hridoy joined Shadman in a crucial stand, mixing caution with attacking strokes as the pair added 88 runs. However, the heat and humidity took their toll. Troubled by cramps in his left leg, Hridoy was stretchered off on 42 from 84 balls in the 66th over.

Litton Das, returning after a hip injury, was unbeaten on 10 when bad light first stopped play at 3:16pm. After a 50-minute delay, the players returned, but another interruption at 4:22pm ended the day. Shadman moved from 96 to 99 in between, unable to find the single that would have brought his century.
Jomel Warrican finished with 2 for 33, while Jayden Seales took one wicket. Debutant Joshua Bishop went wicketless but found sharp turn.
caption:

Bangladesh finished on 213-3 against the West Indies.

headline_marked: Dengue death toll [[crosses 400 mark]] as 9 more die in 24 hours
headline: Dengue death toll crosses 400 mark as 9 more die in 24 hours
summary: Nearly 2,000 people were hospitalized in a single day as the annual dengue death toll in Bangladesh continues to rise.
details: Nine people died from dengue in the last 24 hours, according to a report from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
This brings the total number of deaths from the virus this year to 409.
In the same 24-hour period, 1,982 people were admitted to hospitals across the country.
The total number of hospitalizations for dengue this year has now reached 130,219.
The DGHS report noted that the highest single-day death toll was 11 people, recorded yesterday.
Other significant spikes in deaths occurred on October 6 and 15, when 10 people died in a single day.
caption:
Dengue deaths in Bangladesh have now crossed 400 this year. 9 people died in the last 24 hours alone.

Nine people died from dengue in the last 24 hours, according to a report from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

This brings the total number of deaths from the virus this year to 409.

In the same 24-hour period, 1,982 people were admitted to hospitals across the country.

The total number of hospitalizations for dengue this year has now reached 130,219.

The DGHS report noted that the highest single-day death toll was 11 people, recorded yesterday.

Other significant spikes in deaths occurred on October 6 and 15, when 10 people died in a single day.
